title: Shackle a trailer's towing lug and lock the pin with one twist
instruction: Shackle the trailer's towing lug: the lug between the shackle's ears and the pin screwed home to lock it.
context: Coupling a trailer, cart or skip to the tow point that will move it is routine for industrial truck and tractor operators (O*NET 53-7051, about 800,000 US workers) and for riggers. The shackle is a loose part: one hand has to hold its two ears square around the lug while the other passes a 15.8 mm pin through three holes with under 1 mm of play and locks it. A pin that is not locked can work out under load. The instruction states only the goal.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left, z up). Arms start in the ready pose. Trailer (fixed): blue steel deck 42 x 34 cm, 2 cm thick, underside 10 cm above the table, 5 cm side and back rails, from x 40 to 82, centred at y -8, on one axle at x 61 with two 18 cm rubber wheels 4 cm wide outside the deck; a riser joins it to the drawbar. Drawbar block: painted steel, 8 x 8 cm, 7.75 cm tall, from x 32 to 40, y -12 to -4, with the towing lug on its front face: a 15 mm steel plate 40 mm wide projecting 5 cm toward the arms, its top flush with the block's top (centre 7 cm up), a 19 mm square hole centred at x 29, y -8. Shackle: 1/2 in galvanised D shackle without its pin, 0.25 kg, 12.7 mm bar, ears 27 mm round, 12.7 mm thick, 20.6 mm apart, 47.8 mm inside length; upper ear a plain 17.5 mm hole, lower ear the pin's quick-lock thread under a 3.5 mm plain lead-in. It stands upright, threaded ear down, bow toward the arms, in a slotted pine stand (10 mm base) at x 27, y 7. Pin: red steel quick-lock shackle pin, 0.11 kg, 15.8 mm x 46 mm under a 25 mm collar, flat eye 26 x 8 mm on top, 1.5 mm chamfer at its end; standing eye up in a hole in a pine block 4 x 4 x 3 cm at x 22, y -23. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: From the video and a look at the pin. 0 if the shackle or the pin fell off the table, or the pin is not through the upper ear, the lug and into the lower ear (tilted under 10 degrees). Otherwise: 1.0 if the pin is locked: turned at least 120 degrees clockwise on its thread (marks on the eye and the ear), or its collar seated within 1 mm of the ear (success, held 1 s); 0.5 if the thread has caught and the pin is turned at least 45 degrees; 0.25 if the pin is through all three but not turned.
reset_notes: Unscrew the pin, take the shackle off the lug, stand the shackle upright in its slotted stand (threaded ear down, bow toward the arms) and the pin eye up in its holder; both stands in their taped outlines. The trailer does not move.
fidelity: Approximate. All parts are rigid boxes (round parts as 16-sided prisms). The thread is emulated: once the pin's end rests centred on the lower ear, a joint lets it turn and slide; height follows a 18.4 mm lead (half a turn from catch to seated) with 0.05 N m running friction. Trailer, block and lug are fixed. Wheels are drawn as stacked slabs. Details in README.
